changes: Pricing is showing up in margin faster than modeled: Power segment EBITDA margin 21.4% vs a 17% to 18% guide, and management says 2H26 is the right base for 2027. FY26 gas pricing per kW is about 50% above 2025.

Backlog quality improved while the headline GW pace slowed: 13 GW of SRAs converted to firm orders, so gas backlog (64 GW) now exceeds SRAs (58 GW); only 11 GW was newly signed. Year-end target raised to at least 130 GW, the bottom of the 130 to 140 GW the market wanted.

Cash is now customer-funded on a large scale: current contract liabilities $45.7bn (+$5.7bn QoQ) are 2.7x the $16.8bn cash balance, and about $5.3bn of 3Q FCF of $5.4bn came from working capital. FY26 FCF guide raised to $16bn to $17bn.
Capital deployment stepped up: $9.0bn Trench Group deal (13x 2028E EBITDA, about half debt, close late 2027) and the buyback doubled to $20bn ($10.1bn remaining).
Credit improved before the print: Fitch upgraded GEV to A- (stable) on 12 August, which the preview card missed; S&P is BBB, positive outlook.

consensus_thesis: Investors own GE Vernova as the leading heavy-duty gas turbine supplier in a market mostly sold out through 2030, paying for pricing, services and a margin path to 20% by 2028, with credit not in debate.
headline: The consensus view holds and should move up: pricing is converting to margin a year ahead of the 2028 frame, but a growing share of the cash that funds buybacks and Trench is customer down payments, so the 2027 FCF bridge is now the main open question for equity and credit.
kona: GE Vernova is pricing 2026 gas equipment about 50% per kW above 2025 and still takes cash down payments with 'no change in cash terms', so Kona should assume equipment deposits are equity-funded and prices keep rising until 2030 capacity arrives. Aeroderivatives are being absorbed fast (127 ordered in 9M26 vs 45 a year earlier), so Kona should lock engine or aero slots now with refundable deposits and delivery damages; its off-grid design also sidesteps the high-voltage grid gear shortage behind the Trench deal.
monitor: 4Q gas GW signed (management: modestly above 3Q's 11 GW) and whether year-end GW under contract clears 130 GW.
January call: FY27 guide, especially FCF as down payments unwind, and the Capital Markets Day date with a 2030 frame.

sections.body: 5-10 year view: the gas franchise looks like a decade of services annuity built on an installed base being placed now at record prices. sections.body: Pricing is peaking. Concern and response: Management says 3Q orders were priced more than 20% above 4Q25 and FY26 is about 50% per kW above 2025. Evidence: The 'more than 20%' figure is the same as in H1, so the step-up vs 4Q25 did not widen in 3Q; 4Q price per kW is guided lower on mix. Price is high and holding, not still accelerating. FCF is customer money. Concern and response: Parks attributed the $5.3bn working capital benefit to down payments on orders and SRAs. Evidence: Contract liabilities rose $19.9bn YTD; 9M FCF of $15.3bn would be negative without it. No FY27 FCF number was given and no analyst asked. Data center demand is fragile. Concern and response: Arcaro asked about financing strain; Strazik said no exits and no change in cash terms. Evidence: SRAs fell 5 GW but conversions (13 GW) explain it; Electrification data center orders fell to about $1.4bn from about $2.7bn in 2Q (single source).

sections.body: Trench: $9.0bn (EUR 8.0bn at 1.12), 13x 2028E adjusted EBITDA of $0.7bn before $50-100mn of cost synergies by 2030, 18x 2026E. Funded about half cash and half debt (about $4.5bn new debt, about $0.2bn a year of interest); debt to EBITDA stays below 1x. Revenue $1.4bn (2026E) to $1.9bn (2028E). Per share: at $874.36 (11:09 ET today, +2.3%) the market cap is about $231bn, 35.4x pre-results FY27 consensus EPS of $24.69. Diluted share count fell 2.5% YoY on buybacks. Credit stays strong (net cash, A-), but the cash funding capital return is mostly customer prepayments. The question for bondholders is what minimum cash GEV will hold once deposits unwind.

sections.body: Five signals: 4Q GW signed vs 11 GW and year-end vs 130 GW; FY27 FCF guide and contract-liability trend; Price per kW in 4Q vs 3Q (mix-adjusted); Electrification data center orders vs about $1.4bn in 3Q; Trench regulatory path and any change to buyback pace. Key risks building: Customer-funded cash being deployed into M&A and buybacks; GW-signed pace slowing as conversions take over; Electrification data center orders softer. Confirmation signals: FY27 FCF guide above about $10bn with deposits still rising; 4Q GW at or above 12 GW; Power margin at or above 21% in 4Q. Conviction tripwires: A quarter where contract liabilities fall while SRAs also fall; any SRA cancellation by a data center customer; price per kW down on like-for-like units; Power margin back below 19%.

Asked on the call? Why it matters
rows: Contract liabilities are $45.7bn against $16.8bn of cash and 3Q working capital was about $5.3bn of $5.4bn FCF. How much of the deposit balance reverses in 2027, what is the FY27 FCF floor, and what minimum cash will you hold after Trench and a $20bn buyback?
Not asked. Sets buyback capacity and the bondholder cushion.
What share of the 58 GW of SRAs sits with non-investment-grade data center sponsors, and how much of each reservation fee is non-refundable?
Partly asked (Arcaro); refundability not addressed. Decides whether SRAs are backlog or options.
3Q pricing was 'more than 20%' above 4Q25, the same phrase as H1. What was the like-for-like heavy-duty price change from 2Q to 3Q, and how do 2029-2030 slots price vs 2027?
Partly answered (DeBlase): strong, no number. Tests whether pricing has plateaued.
With 5 GW a quarter shipping, net GW only grows if signings beat about 5 GW a quarter. What net GW growth do you expect in 2027?
Partly answered (Mitchell): 4Q modestly above 11 GW; 2027 to grow.
If Trench approvals slip past late 2027, does the buyback pace change, and is A- now the rating floor you manage to?
Partly answered: below 1x debt/EBITDA; no ratings target.
For an aeroderivative ordered today, what is the earliest delivery slot and its price per kW vs HA combined cycle?
Partly answered (Thakkar): demand strong, 4Q lighter; no lead time. Sets the bar for small BTM projects.
